text:
kai: follow-up from the multi-region RFC: concrete ask  we need a single fallback contract when the resident region is unavailable. block, proxy, or escrow? please keep replies short.

viv: short: prefer a conservative default (block) + an explicit opt-in path.

nora: runtime note: proxying writes synchronously to a remote resident store is possible but adds ~200-300ms p99 depending on path. Escrow (async accept) saves latency but adds reconciliation complexity.

legal-bot: reminder: any processing or storage of EU-resident data outside the EU requires tenant-level consent that is auditable. Consent must include scope and timestamp.

ops-oncall: operational constraints: if we accept in standby (escrow) we must monitor queue_age and queue_depth and have an automated cork when > threshold. Also surface an operator marker for stale escrows older than X.

devx: API proposal: X-Residence-Preference: block | proxy-sync | accept-escrow. Default=block. Also return machine-readable error when blocked.

kai: two engineering questions: 1) idempotency for escrows, 2) embeddings/replication gating for pending writes.

nora: idempotency: require request_id/idempotency_key. Escrow record stores request_id, tenant, origin_region, payload_hash, result_ref. Replayer dedupes by request_id.

viv: replication: label embeddings as residency=pending and block replication to non-resident stores until reconciliation marks final. That adds possible search inconsistency which we must document to customers.

legal-bot: consent-service suggestion: issue a timebound consent token format CONSENT::{tenant}::{id}::{ts}::{scopes}. Validation endpoint returns boolean + audit data. Keep consent logs for 7 years.

ops-oncall: metrics to add: residency_forward_attempts, escrow_accept_rate, escrow_replay_failures, consent_check_latency_ms. Set alarm if consent_check_latency_ms > 500ms.

devx: error payload example we should standardize: {"error":"RESIDENCY_BLOCKED","code":"RESIDENCY_NO_CONSENT","help":"Enable cross-region or contact account team"} (returned as single-line JSON in message).

kai: decision proposal: default=block; enterprise opt-in=accept-escrow with consent-token; developer opt-in=proxy-sync for non-sensitive tenants. Who owns impl?

nora: I'll own runtime escrow + idempotency helpers.

devx: I'll own API header + error schema + docs.

ops-oncall: we own runbook + metrics and cork logic.

legal-bot: will publish consent token schema and retention policy.

sam.k: timeline: RFC follow-up PR by Fri, runtime spike for escrow next week. If owners agree, Ill mark RFC as accepted pending PR.

viv: +1 to timeline.

kai: +1 to decision. closing once PR lands. thanks.
